entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Quintus Terentius Scaurus was a Latin grammarian who flourished during the reigns of Trajan and Hadrian.

Born in unknown circumstances, Scaurus was a prominent figure in the Roman Empire's educational circles, known for his expertise in Latin literature and grammar.

As a leading authority on the works of Terence, Scaurus's most notable contribution was the compilation of a comprehensive treatise on Latin rhetoric, which became a cornerstone of Roman educational institutions.

Scaurus's legacy extended beyond the realm of scholarship, as his work on Latin language and literature influenced the development of Roman imperial policies, particularly in the realm of education and cultural exchange.

In the words of the Roman historian Quintus Curtius Rufus, 'Scaurus's writings on Latin rhetoric were so esteemed that they were considered essential reading for Roman magistrates and senators, who sought to emulate his mastery of the language.'

This enduring impact is a testament to Scaurus's significance in the annals of Roman history, where his contributions to the realm of Latin language and literature left an indelible mark.
